item.title: Apple pushes Siri toward agentic AI with new app integration and fine‑grained controls
item.description:
Apple pushes Siri toward agentic AI with new app integration and fine‑grained controls

Apple is updating Siri to become more agentic, adding fine‑grained control over its own apps and integration with third‑party services.

🔍 Overview

  • Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that CEO John Ternus is pressuring AI czar Craig Federighi to accelerate the Siri roadmap.
  • Federighi has delivered a functional version of Siri AI on an incredibly short timeline, but the company acknowledges it is not keeping pace with rivals.
  • Apple is racing to make Siri more agentic and to enable ongoing tasks rather than single‑step commands.

⚙️ Upcoming Features

  • Fine‑grained control of first‑party apps – Siri will be able to rotate and crop images in Photos and organize Safari tabs. Expected with iOS 27.3.
  • Third‑party app integration – Siri will place orders through Grubhub, book reservations through OpenTable, and similar actions. Expected in the Spring following iOS 27.3.

📅 Timeline

Feature Expected Release
First‑party app control (Photos, Safari) iOS 27.3
Third‑party app integration (Grubhub, OpenTable) Spring after iOS 27.3

💡 Why it matters

  • Competitors such as OpenAI’s Dots, Meta’s Muse, and Grok can keep track of goals and continue pursuing objectives without the user initiating every step.
  • Apple aims to give Siri similar agentic capabilities, allowing it to perform ongoing tasks and manage objectives, a direction the company may reach as early as next year.

#Apple #Siri #AIagents #VoiceAssistants

Source: Apple is racing to make Siri more agentic

item.title: Apple Releases watchOS 27.3 Beta Featuring Siri Audio Intelligence
item.description:
Apple Releases watchOS 27.3 Beta Featuring Siri Audio Intelligence

Apple has introduced the watchOS 27.3 developer beta, which enables Siri to utilize the Apple Watch’s microphone for new Audio Intelligence features. This update includes Siri Recap and Live Rewind, which utilize “ambient listening” to summarize or transcribe audio detected by the device.

🧩 How it works

The new Audio Intelligence tools allow Siri to process conversation audio for immediate recall or later review:

Feature Functionality
Siri Recap Uses ambient listening to generate high-level summaries, titles, and key points of conversations in the Siri app.
Live Rewind Generates a text snippet of the last 15 seconds of detected audio for users to catch missed information.

Users can activate Live Rewind by double-pressing the Digital Crown to display a text snippet of a conversation. Users can then ask Siri about the content of that text or save it to the Siri app. When Siri Recap is enabled, Apple Intelligence automatically generates a title and key points after a conversation concludes.

⚙️ Key details

Apple released an Audio Intelligence Privacy Overview detailing how user data is protected during around-the-clock listening. According to the documentation:

  • Raw audio is handled within dedicated hardware and is not saved as a file.
  • Audio data is not accessible to the operating system, apps, or Apple.
  • Saved summaries and snippets are end-to-end encrypted when synced across devices for users with iCloud two-factor authentication and a device passcode.

Additionally, a redesigned Health app is available for testing in the iOS 27.3 developer beta. It includes an Insights tab for heart, sleep, and fitness summaries, a For You section with personalized recommendations, and educational health content.

🚀 Availability

The watchOS 27.3 and iOS 27.3 developer betas are rolling out now. The update includes expanded language support for global English, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), French, Japanese, Korean, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Turkish, and Vietnamese.

#AppleWatch #watchOS #Siri #AppleIntelligence

Source: Apple’s latest watchOS beta includes its new always-on Audio Intelligence features

item.title: Apple Highlights AI Growth on Record‑Breaking Earnings Call
item.description:
Apple Highlights AI Growth on Record‑Breaking Earnings Call

Apple’s fiscal‑year earnings call featured AI more prominently than any prior quarter, signaling how the company plans to weave intelligence into its products and revenue streams.

🔍 Overview

  • AI and Apple Intelligence were mentioned a record 45 times on the call, surpassing the count after the June 2024 Siri revamp.
  • CFO Kevan Parekh and CEO John Ternus both emphasized a “tremendous opportunity in AI” for future growth.

📊 Financial Context

  • Apple posted its best‑ever fiscal year for revenue and earnings per share.
  • iPhone revenue rose 17.5 % YoY to a September‑quarter record $57.6 B.
  • Mac revenue climbed 24 % to $10.8 B, the highest in four years.
  • Shares fell in pre‑market trading after Apple warned that rising memory costs could squeeze profit margins in the holiday quarter.
  • Operating expenses increased 21 % to $19.2 B, reflecting higher R&D spending, including on AI.
  • Capital expenditures were $2.2 B, a fraction of peers such as Amazon ($77.3 B) and Alphabet ($51.4 B).

🤖 AI Strategy

  • Apple’s approach blends on‑device processing, its own servers, and outside AI technology.
  • Siri AI uses models developed with Google’s Gemini technology.
  • Apple plans to let users choose among outside AI providers for features like writing tools and image generation.
  • Parekh said it is “too early to predict how many requests will require servers rather than on‑device processing.”
  • Siri AI’s cloud costs will appear in services cost of sales.

🚀 Product Rollout

  • The revamped assistant launched in beta for US English users in September, then expanded to French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish in October.
  • Ternus noted that server‑side features, including Siri AI and intelligent photo editing, will have usage limits.
  • Customers needing more capacity “will be able to purchase expanded access in the future.”

🖥️ Local AI on Macs

Device Local AI Use Partner / Note
Mac Mini Loss‑prevention across hundreds of Gap stores, avoiding cloud token costs Gap
Mac Studio Pricing‑estimate workflows for Christie’s, improving efficiency Christie’s
iPhone AI‑driven features provide a compelling reason to upgrade and switch devices –
Siri AI Server‑side model with usage limits; cloud costs counted in services cost of sales –

💰 Revenue Opportunities

  • Parekh cited a “wide range of ways that AI can contribute to revenue growth over time.”
  • He added that AI offers “a compelling reason for customers to upgrade and switch in order to get the latest capabilities.”
  • He also highlighted “opportunities across third‑party apps and partnerships as well as first‑party opportunities.”
  • The Wall Street Journal reported Apple is on pace to earn more than $1 B in App Store fees from generative‑AI apps by 2026 (AppMagic).

⚠️ Challenges & Cost Pressures

  • Memory‑cost inflation may compress margins in the upcoming holiday quarter.
  • Predicting the split between on‑device and server processing remains uncertain.
  • Apple’s capital spending on AI infrastructure remains modest compared to its big‑tech peers.

#Apple #AI #Siri #GenerativeAI

Source: Apple is all in on AI — its own and everyone else’s

item.title: Apple Settles Class Action Lawsuit Over AI-Upgraded Siri Rollout Delays
item.description:
Apple Settles Class Action Lawsuit Over AI-Upgraded Siri Rollout Delays

Apple has agreed to a $250 million settlement to resolve claims that the company failed to deliver an AI-upgraded version of Siri as expected. While Apple denies any wrongdoing, the settlement allows eligible iPhone owners to submit claims for a payout.

⚙️ Key details

The class action lawsuit alleged that Apple established a clear consumer expectation that AI features showcased at WWDC 2024 would be available upon the launch of the iPhone 16. Although marketed as “built for Apple Intelligence,” the devices launched with a more limited set of capabilities. The promised AI-upgraded Siri was subsequently delayed and only released recently with iOS 27.

🚀 Eligibility and Claims

Individuals who purchased specific iPhone models in the United States between June 10, 2024, and March 29, 2025, are eligible to participate. To file a claim, users must provide their name, contact information, and device serial number on the settlement website by December 21, 2026.

Eligible Device Model
iPhone 15 Pro
iPhone 15 Pro Max
iPhone 16 models

💰 Payout Information

The estimated payout is $25 per eligible device. However, this amount may increase to as much as $95 depending on the total volume of claims submitted.

#Apple #Siri #AppleIntelligence #ClassAction #Lawsuit

Source: iPhone owners can now submit claims in Apple’s $250 million Siri AI settlement

item.title: Apple Introduces Siri Audio Intelligence Features with On‑Device Privacy Protections
item.description:
Apple Introduces Siri Audio Intelligence Features with On‑Device Privacy Protections

Apple announced a handful of new Siri AI Audio Intelligence features — Siri Recap, Live Rewind, Sound Recognition, and Music Recognition — at the iPhone Duo launch event, accompanied by a privacy‑focused technical document.

🔍 Overview

  • Siri Recap – summarizes recent interactions.
  • Live Rewind – lets users double‑tap the Digital Crown to replay recent audio.
  • Sound Recognition – identifies ambient sounds.
  • Music Recognition – detects music playing nearby.

🧩 How it works

  • Audio is captured by the microphone and immediately routed into the Secure Enclave of the S11 chip found in Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4.
  • The Secure Enclave is a hardware‑isolated compartment that processes sensor data separately from the rest of the system.
  • Within the Enclave, audio is analyzed for speech, sounds, or music without transcribing or storing the raw audio.
  • Processed data lives in a continuously overwritten buffer that never creates an audio recording and is not saved as a file.
  • If results need to move to an iPhone, they are encrypted and transferred through the Secure Enclaves of both devices.

⚙️ Key details

  • The raw audio is not accessible to the operating system, apps, or Apple.
  • Users control when Audio Intelligence features are active; for example, Live Rewind requires a double‑tap of the Digital Crown each time.
  • Users decide what text to keep from Siri Recap and Live Rewind.
  • Kept text syncs with end‑to‑end encryption when a device passcode and iCloud two‑factor authentication are enabled.
  • Apple states it cannot access users’ raw audio from these features.

#Apple #Siri #AudioIntelligence #Privacy

Source: Read the Apple document explaining how new listening features still protect your privacy
